sourceBindings.text: Complete a one-page report from your own supervised Plot C work. State what your pH and texture evidence supports, suggest two conditional crop candidates and at least one management next step. A report, self-rating or second attempt cannot substitute for observed practical competence.

Submit a one-page Plot C report identifying the sample, date, purpose, real pH and texture method/results, interpretation, two conditional crop candidates and at least one supported management action with limitations.

Compare personal data with the separate pH 6.8/loam and pH 5.8/sandy-loam models, state what pH and texture alone cannot prove, and trace every final-review task to its own answer or performance evidence.
Use specific feedback to practise the affected skill and submit a new performance record; allow another 'not yet demonstrated' decision if a criterion is still missing.
Read the course result as a combination of online knowledge evidence and individually observed practical evidence, with each unobserved skill left visibly unassessed.

sourceBindings.text: Arrange a Plot C one-page report, inserting only your own observed pH and texture records and marking any still-missing method or date.
Choose two crop candidates and one management next step, then state the unmeasured limits and distinguish the pH 6.8 model from your sample.

Sort final-review evidence into an answer, written product or individually observed process. Then draft the source's five-point team safety checklist covering PPE and emergency preparedness; its content needs review and the real site still needs the trainer's inspection.
Given an invalid calibration result, write specific feedback, practice and a new assessment record that can still be unpassed.
Explain the missing evidence or reasoning, link to the affected explanation and permit directed retry without a false practical pass.

This workspace saves drafts. Text presence, a model value, a quiz score and a self-rating do not approve the final report, verify one printed page or establish practical competence. An assessor must review the actual evidence and reasoning. Missing own-sample pH or texture leaves the actual-results report pending; practical records remain separately unobserved.

Self-assessment 5.2 supports reflection about reporting. Its Can / Cannot / Partly choices and notes do not approve a report or establish practical competence. Reflect on what still needs practice; actual assessment requires separate individual evidence.

sourceBindings.text: preliminary report
A concise interpretation of available evidence with its limits, not a certificate of complete soil health.
reassessment
A new assessment after specific feedback and practice, with a new actual decision rather than an automatic pass.
competent
The relevant skill was observed safely and accurately against its stated practical standard.
not yet demonstrated
Required evidence is incomplete or did not meet the criterion; targeted practice and another genuine observation may follow.
data provenance
The record linking a value to the learner’s sample, date, method, instrument and person who performed the work.
crop candidate
A possible crop based on current evidence, requiring checks of climate, water, drainage and nutrients before a planting decision.
